title: Are US Long Bonds A Buy? (Part II)

Are US Long Bonds A Buy? (Part II)

Will Denyer

Gavekal Research | 2 Sep 2026

The US Treasury plans to buy back more debt at the long end of the curve and issue more at the short end. If Scott Bessent pursues this “Treasury twist” aggressively enough, the Treasury secretary could succeed in weighing on long-term yields and flattening the yield curve (see Are US Long Bonds A Buy? (Part I)). But he will have his work cut out; there are numerous forces working to push the long end higher. First, while the Treasury is trying to reduce the supply of long-term debt in the market with its twist, the Federal Reserve is gradually “untwisting” its own balance sheet away from long-term securities, leaving more duration for the market to digest. Speaking at Jackson Hole last Friday, Fed chair Kevin Warsh gave no indication that he intends to change course and join the Treasury in buying long-term securities. Quite the contrary (see A DTR Moment For The Fed And Treasury). Only time will tell whether the Treasury will twist faster than the Fed untwists; all eyes will be on the scale of the Treasury’s first expanded buyback on September 9.
